{
  "cmd": "gh issue create --repo blackgirlbytes/planetfall-seed-signalkit --title \"Explore Marvin as an NPC or player avatar\" --body-file - <<'EOF'\n## Problem\nMarvin currently exists mostly as terminal/dialogue presence. The game is first-person, so the player never sees themself, and Marvin does not yet have an embodied role in the world.\n\nThere was a suggestion to make Marvin more present as a character: either as an NPC the player encounters, or as a representation of the player when the game leaves first-person view.\n\n## Why this matters\n- Marvin is one of the strongest character/brand hooks in the game, but right now that personality is mostly delivered through text.\n- A visible Marvin presence could make the world feel less abstract and give players a clearer emotional anchor.\n- If the player ever exits first-person or enters an external/cinematic view, Marvin could help avoid the awkwardness of an invisible protagonist.\n- This could reinforce the Entire connection without adding more tutorial copy.\n\n## Design directions to explore\n- Marvin as an NPC: a guide, ship AI, terminal avatar, drone, projection, or companion that appears at key moments.\n- Marvin as player representation: if the camera leaves first-person, the visible body/avatar could be Marvin or a Marvin-like operator.\n- Marvin as an interaction layer: a diegetic helper who comments on `entire` commands, dispatches, checkpoints, or failures.\n- Marvin as only a visual motif: keep first-person gameplay, but use brief appearances, portraits, holograms, or interface marks.\n\n## Open questions\n- Is Marvin meant to be the player, a separate guide, or the voice of the tooling?\n- Should Marvin appear during gameplay, only in transitions, or only in terminal/UI moments?\n- Would a visible character improve clarity, or would it distract from the first-person immersion?\n- What visual language should Marvin use so it fits Planetfall's tone and does not feel like unrelated branding pasted on top?\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n- Decide whether Marvin should be an NPC, a player avatar, a UI/terminal presence, or remain text-only.\n- If embodied, define where Marvin appears and what gameplay/narrative job that appearance serves.\n- If the player can leave first-person view, define what the player sees and whether Marvin represents that view.\n- Document the chosen direction before implementation so art, camera, and UX work stay aligned.\n\nRelated: #6\nEOF",

---
name: github
description: Triage and orient GitHub repository, pull request, and issue work through the connected GitHub app. Use when the user asks for general GitHub help, wants PR or issue summaries, or needs repository context before choosing a more specific GitHub workflow.
---

# GitHub

## Overview

Use this skill as the umbrella entrypoint for general GitHub work in this plugin. It should decide whether the task stays in repo and PR triage or should be handed off to a more specific review, CI, or publish workflow.

This plugin is intentionally hybrid:

- Prefer the GitHub app from this plugin for repository, issue, pull request, comment, label, reaction, and PR creation workflows.
- Use local `git` and `gh` only when the connector does not cover the job well, especially for current-branch PR discovery, branch creation, commit and push, `gh auth status`, and GitHub Actions log inspection.
- Keep connector state and local checkout context aligned. If the request is about the current branch, resolve the local repo and branch before acting.

Once the intent is clear, route to the specialist skill immediately and do not keep broad GitHub triage in scope longer than needed.

## Connector-First Responsibilities

Handle these directly in this skill when the request does not need a narrower specialist workflow:

- repository orientation once the repo, PR, issue, or local checkout is identified
- recent PR or issue triage
- PR metadata summaries
- PR patch inspection
- PR comments, labels, and reactions
- issue lookup and summarization
- PR creation after a branch is already pushed

Prefer the GitHub app from this plugin for those flows because it provides structured PR, issue, and review-adjacent data without depending on a local checkout. If the repository is not already identifiable from the user request or local git context, ask for the repo instead of pretending there is a repo-search flow that may not exist.

## Routing Rules

1. Resolve the operating context first:
   - If the user provides a repository, PR number, issue number, or URL, use that.
   - If the request is about "this branch" or "the current PR", resolve local git context and use `gh` only as needed to discover the branch PR.
   - If the repository is still ambiguous after local inspection, ask for the repo identifier.
2. Classify the request before taking action:
   - `repo or PR triage`: summarize PRs, issues, patches, comments, labels, reactions, or repository state
   - `review follow-up`: unresolved review threads, requested changes, or inline review feedback
   - `CI debugging`: failing checks, Actions logs, or CI root-cause analysis
   - `publish changes`: create or switch branches, stage changes, commit, push, and open a draft PR
3. Route to the specialist skill as soon as the category is clear:
   - Review comments and requested changes: `../gh-address-comments/SKILL.md`
   - Failing GitHub Actions checks: `../gh-fix-ci/SKILL.md`
   - Commit, push, and open PR: `../yeet/SKILL.md`
4. Keep the hybrid model consistent after routing:
   - connector first for PR and issue data
   - local `git` and `gh` only for the specific gaps the connector does not cover

## Default Workflow

1. Resolve repository and item scope.
2. Gather structured PR or issue context through the GitHub app from this plugin.
3. Decide whether the task stays in connector-backed triage or needs a specialist skill.
4. Route immediately when the work becomes review follow-up, CI debugging, or publish workflow.
5. End with a clear summary of what was inspected, what changed, and what remains.

## Output Expectations

- For triage requests, return a concise summary of the repository, PR, or issue state and the next likely action.
- For mixed requests, tell the user which specialist path you are taking and why.
- For connector-backed write actions, restate the exact PR, issue, label, or reaction target before applying the change.
- Never imply that GitHub Actions logs are available through the connector alone. That remains a `gh` workflow.

## Examples

- "Use GitHub to summarize the open PRs in this repo and tell me what needs attention."
- "Help with this PR."
- "Review the latest comments on PR 482 and tell me what is actionable."
- "Debug the failing checks on this branch."
- "Commit these changes, push them, and open a draft PR."

The submitted `score` value itself is not directly trusted, but the API currently trusts enough client-supplied scoring inputs that a forged request can still inflate the server-computed score.\n\nObserved report: a Level 3 win payload with impossible progress values was accepted and produced a score around `1,234,567,890`.\n\n## Why this matters\n- Leaderboard rankings can be polluted by fabricated scores.\n- Honest players lose trust in the leaderboard if impossible runs can be submitted.\n- Recomputing the score on the server is not sufficient if the server recomputes from untrusted client fields.\n- Once fake high scores are written, they may need manual cleanup from the database.\n\n## Likely root cause\n`api/leaderboard.js` recomputes `score`, but `validateEntry()` accepts client-provided values such as `progressCompleted`, `progressTotal`, `timeRemaining`, `durationSeconds`, and `mistakes` with minimal bounds. `computeScore()` then awards extra progress points for `progressCompleted > progressTotal`, so an impossible `progressCompleted` value can generate an impossible score.\n\nRelevant code paths:\n- `api/leaderboard.js`: `validateEntry()` reads submission fields.\n- `api/leaderboard.js`: `computeScore()` calculates `extraProgress` from client-provided progress.\n- Database checks only require non-negative values, not gameplay-valid maximums.\n\n## Suggested fixes\n- Reject submissions where progress exceeds the known maximum for the submitted level/outcome.\n- Clamp or remove `extraProgress` unless it maps to a real, bounded game mechanic.\n- Validate `timeRemaining`, `durationSeconds`, and `mistakes` against plausible per-level bounds.\n- Consider deriving accepted run stats from a server-issued/signed run token instead of trusting raw client payloads.\n- Add API tests for forged leaderboard payloads, including huge progress, invalid totals, impossible wins, negative/overflow-ish values, and suspicious time values.\n- Consider a one-time cleanup path for any existing impossible leaderboard rows.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n- A forged submission with impossible progress cannot create a high score.\n- The server rejects or safely clamps out-of-range leaderboard fields before scoring.\n- Automated tests cover the reported exploit class.\n- Existing valid game submissions still save name: github
description: Triage and orient GitHub repository, pull request, and issue work through the connected GitHub app. Use when the user asks for general GitHub help, wants PR or issue summaries, or needs repository context before choosing a more specific GitHub workflow.
---

# GitHub

## Overview

Use this skill as the umbrella entrypoint for general GitHub work in this plugin. It should decide whether the task stays in repo and PR triage or should be handed off to a more specific review, CI, or publish workflow.

This plugin is intentionally hybrid:

- Prefer the GitHub app from this plugin for repository, issue, pull request, comment, label, reaction, and PR creation workflows.
- Use local `git` and `gh` only when the connector does not cover the job well, especially for current-branch PR discovery, branch creation, commit and push, `gh auth status`, and GitHub Actions log inspection.
- Keep connector state and local checkout context aligned. If the request is about the current branch, resolve the local repo and branch before acting.

Once the intent is clear, route to the specialist skill immediately and do not keep broad GitHub triage in scope longer than needed.

## Connector-First Responsibilities

Handle these directly in this skill when the request does not need a narrower specialist workflow:

- repository orientation once the repo, PR, issue, or local checkout is identified
- recent PR or issue triage
- PR metadata summaries
- PR patch inspection
- PR comments, labels, and reactions
- issue lookup and summarization
- PR creation after a branch is already pushed

Prefer the GitHub app from this plugin for those flows because it provides structured PR, issue, and review-adjacent data without depending on a local checkout. If the repository is not already identifiable from the user request or local git context, ask for the repo instead of pretending there is a repo-search flow that may not exist.

## Routing Rules

1. Resolve the operating context first:
   - If the user provides a repository, PR number, issue number, or URL, use that.
   - If the request is about "this branch" or "the current PR", resolve local git context and use `gh` only as needed to discover the branch PR.
   - If the repository is still ambiguous after local inspection, ask for the repo identifier.
2. Classify the request before taking action:
   - `repo or PR triage`: summarize PRs, issues, patches, comments, labels, reactions, or repository state
   - `review follow-up`: unresolved review threads, requested changes, or inline review feedback
   - `CI debugging`: failing checks, Actions logs, or CI root-cause analysis
   - `publish changes`: create or switch branches, stage changes, commit, push, and open a draft PR
3. Route to the specialist skill as soon as the category is clear:
   - Review comments and requested changes: `../gh-address-comments/SKILL.md`
   - Failing GitHub Actions checks: `../gh-fix-ci/SKILL.md`
   - Commit, push, and open PR: `../yeet/SKILL.md`
4. Keep the hybrid model consistent after routing:
   - connector first for PR and issue data
   - local `git` and `gh` only for the specific gaps the connector does not cover

## Default Workflow

1. Resolve repository and item scope.
2. Gather structured PR or issue context through the GitHub app from this plugin.
3. Decide whether the task stays in connector-backed triage or needs a specialist skill.
4. Route immediately when the work becomes review follow-up, CI debugging, or publish workflow.
5. End with a clear summary of what was inspected, what changed, and what remains.

## Output Expectations

- For triage requests, return a concise summary of the repository, PR, or issue state and the next likely action.
- For mixed requests, tell the user which specialist path you are taking and why.
- For connector-backed write actions, restate the exact PR, issue, label, or reaction target before applying the change.
- Never imply that GitHub Actions logs are available through the connector alone. That remains a `gh` workflow.

## Examples

- "Use GitHub to summarize the open PRs in this repo and tell me what needs attention."
- "Help with this PR."
- "Review the latest comments on PR 482 and tell me what is actionable."
- "Debug the failing checks on this branch."
- "Commit these changes, push them, and open a draft PR."

# GitHub

## Overview

Use this skill as the umbrella entrypoint for general GitHub work in this plugin. It should decide whether the task stays in repo and PR triage or should be handed off to a more specific review, CI, or publish workflow.

This plugin is intentionally hybrid:

- Prefer the GitHub app from this plugin for repository, issue, pull request, comment, label, reaction, and PR creation workflows.
- Use local `git` and `gh` only when the connector does not cover the job well, especially for current-branch PR discovery, branch creation, commit and push, `gh auth status`, and GitHub Actions log inspection.
- Keep connector state and local checkout context aligned. If the request is about the current branch, resolve the local repo and branch before acting.

Once the intent is clear, route to the specialist skill immediately and do not keep broad GitHub triage in scope longer than needed.

## Connector-First Responsibilities

Handle these directly in this skill when the request does not need a narrower specialist workflow:

- repository orientation once the repo, PR, issue, or local checkout is identified
- recent PR or issue triage
- PR metadata summaries
- PR patch inspection
- PR comments, labels, and reactions
- issue lookup and summarization
- PR creation after a branch is already pushed

Prefer the GitHub app from this plugin for those flows because it provides structured PR, issue, and review-adjacent data without depending on a local checkout. If the repository is not already identifiable from the user request or local git context, ask for the repo instead of pretending there is a repo-search flow that may not exist.

## Routing Rules

1. Resolve the operating context first:
   - If the user provides a repository, PR number, issue number, or URL, use that.
   - If the request is about "this branch" or "the current PR", resolve local git context and use `gh` only as needed to discover the branch PR.
   - If the repository is still ambiguous after local inspection, ask for the repo identifier.
2. Classify the request before taking action:
   - `repo or PR triage`: summarize PRs, issues, patches, comments, labels, reactions, or repository state
   - `review follow-up`: unresolved review threads, requested changes, or inline review feedback
   - `CI debugging`: failing checks, Actions logs, or CI root-cause analysis
   - `publish changes`: create or switch branches, stage changes, commit, push, and open a draft PR
3. Route to the specialist skill as soon as the category is clear:
   - Review comments and requested changes: `../gh-address-comments/SKILL.md`
   - Failing GitHub Actions checks: `../gh-fix-ci/SKILL.md`
   - Commit, push, and open PR: `../yeet/SKILL.md`
4. Keep the hybrid model consistent after routing:
   - connector first for PR and issue data
   - local `git` and `gh` only for the specific gaps the connector does not cover

## Default Workflow

1. Resolve repository and item scope.
2. Gather structured PR or issue context through the GitHub app from this plugin.
3. Decide whether the task stays in connector-backed triage or needs a specialist skill.
4. Route immediately when the work becomes review follow-up, CI debugging, or publish workflow.
5. End with a clear summary of what was inspected, what changed, and what remains.

## Output Expectations

- For triage requests, return a concise summary of the repository, PR, or issue state and the next likely action.
- For mixed requests, tell the user which specialist path you are taking and why.
- For connector-backed write actions, restate the exact PR, issue, label, or reaction target before applying the change.
- Never imply that GitHub Actions logs are available through the connector alone. That remains a `gh` workflow.

## Examples

- "Use GitHub to summarize the open PRs in this repo and tell me what needs attention."
- "Help with this PR."
- "Review the latest comments on PR 482 and tell me what is actionable."
- "Debug the failing checks on this branch."
- "Commit these changes, push them, and open a draft PR."

There does not appear to be an upsert, uniqueness rule, or retention policy for a normalized player identity/personal best.\n\nRelevant code paths:\n- `api/leaderboard.js`: `leaderboard_entries` table schema\n- `api/leaderboard.js`: POST handler inserts every validated submission into `leaderboard_entries`\n- `api/leaderboard.js`: leaderboard query ranks rows, not distinct players/personal bests\n\n## Suggested fixes\n- Decide the intended leaderboard model: best score per normalized username, best score per username per level/outcome, or a separate history table plus public best table.\n- Normalize usernames consistently before comparing records, likely case-insensitive and trimmed.\n- On save, update the existing personal-best row only if the new run beats the stored score/tie-breakers.\n- Keep lower duplicate runs out of the public top 10, or store them separately with a retention limit if run history is desired.\n- Add a cleanup/migration for existing duplicate rows.\n- Add tests for repeated saves by the same username, lower score submissions, higher score submissions, and tie-breakers.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n- Re-saving with the same normalized username does not create duplicate public leaderboard rows.\n- A new higher score replaces/updates that player's personal best.\n- A lower score does not overwrite a better personal best.\n- The public top 10 displays the intended distinct set of leaderboard records.\n- Existing duplicate rows are cleaned up or hidden from the public leaderboard.\n\nRelated: #8\nEOF",
